newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Iraq "clear and present danger" to Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Iraq "clear and present danger" to Gulf.

text.p: The U.S. missile attack on Iraq was justified because Iraq's military actions pose a "clear and present danger" to neighboring nations and to the flow of oil, U.S Defense Secretary William Perry said on Tuesday.

"The issue is not simply the Iraqi attack on (the Kurdish town of) Erbil, it is the clear and present danger that (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein poses to his neighbours, the security and stability of the region and the flow of oil to the world," Perry said at a Pentagon briefing on an U.S. missile attack against Iraqi air defence and communications targets.

The strikes were in retaliation for Iraq's attacks against Kurds in the north of Iraqi, in which Baghdad intervened on the side of one Kurdish faction against another. Perry said the United States "reserves the right to conduct future military operations" against Iraq if need be.

Washington announced it was also expanding a no-fly zone enforced by allied warplanes against Iraq in the southern part of the country, from the suburbs of Baghdad to the Kuwaiti border. Perry said the reason for action in that separate area was that Washington sees Saddam's threat as much broader and involving the same neighbours protected by an allied coalition in the 1991 Gulf War including Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Israel.

"Our concern is that if Saddam is emboldened by what he would see as his success in the north, he might strike out in areas which are of greater strategic importance to him as well as to us in the south," Perry said. He said the extension of the southern no-fly zone would commence at noon on Wednesday.
